hook_text: The first photograph took hours to make. Today, your phone can take one in less than a second.
clip_script: An old photo album opens: a family in their best clothes, standing very still, not smiling, in black and white. Turn the page: a colour photo of a wedding, printed from film. Then a phone screen: hundreds of photos, videos and selfies, sent to family in seconds. Next to it, a huge grey phone the size of a brick, from 1973. Cameras and phones started separately. Now they live together in your pocket.
visual_style: Whiteboard split: on one side, a box camera, a film roll and a printed photo; on the other side, a brick phone and a cell tower; both arrows meeting in a modern smartphone.
mood: Fun and surprising, like discovering old family photos.
pacing: Page-turning rhythm through the album, then a quick swipe through the phone gallery.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and ask to see the oldest photograph in your family.
